Repository Architecture

+

The workspace, the data flow, and the testing strategy.

+ +
+

Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root pyproject.toml for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable agentic_odi_* package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.

+

Layout +
apps/
+  cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
+  mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
+  studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
+  studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
+packages/
+  core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
+  connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
+infra/cloudflare/ Worker + Wrangler config for the free-plan deployment
+scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
+tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
+docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
+packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
+

Dependency Direction +
apps/cli ──────────────┐
+apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
+apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
+                                 │
+apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
+
    +
  • packages/core depends on no other workspace package.
    • +
  • packages/connectors depends on core only where it needs shared models.
    • +
  • Every runnable app may depend on core; none of them imports another app.
    • +
  • The React SPA only talks to apps/studio-api over /api; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
    • +
+

Persistence +
    +
  • SQLiteRepository is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
    • +
  • The default database is ~/.agentic-odi/odi.db, overridable with AGENTIC_ODI_DB.
    • +
  • build_repository() chooses SQLite by default and InMemoryRepository when AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:, which is what tests use.
    • +
  • The CLI selects its backend with --backend local|mcp or AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND.
    • +
  • The Studio API selects local (direct service calls) or mcp (passthrough) with AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND or create_app(backend=...).
    • +
+

MCP Contract +

packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py owns ToolName, ToolSpec, TOOL_SPECS, and TOOL_NAMES. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py; the CLI's local handlers are checked by tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py.

+

Entry Points + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
CommandModule
agentic-odiagentic_odi_cli.cli:app
agentic-odi-server / agentic-odi-mcp-serveragentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main
agentic-odi-studio-apiagentic_odi_studio_api.main:main
uv run python scripts/dev.pyDev launcher (MCP + Studio API)

Build

+

CLI Reference

+

Backends, chat, entities, and scoring.

+ +
+

The agentic-odi CLI is a Typer-based +command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It +provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data +commands are local-first: they read and write a SQLite store with no server +required, and switch to a remote MCP server with --backend mcp.

+

Install the workspace first if you have not already:

+
uv sync --all-packages
+

Launching +
python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
+python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
+python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
+

A console script is also installed, so agentic-odi --version works the same way.

+

Global options + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
OptionEnvironment variableDefaultMeaning
--backend local|mcpAGENTIC_ODI_BACKENDlocalRun in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server.
--db PATHAGENTIC_ODI_DB~/.agentic-odi/odi.dbStore path for the local backend.
--mcp-url URLAGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URLhttp://localhost:8000/mcpServer URL for the mcp backend.
+

Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add --json for +machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero +(0 success, 1 error, 2 usage error).

+

Interactive chat +

agentic-odi chat (or simply agentic-odi in a terminal) starts an +offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or +MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service, +and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.

+
agentic-odi chat
+agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
+

Connection settings +

The chat resolves settings in priority order: +CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
VariableDefaultCLI flag
AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URLhttp://localhost:8001/v1--base-url
AGENTIC_ODI_MODELlocal-tools-model--model
AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEYlocal--api-key
AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URLhttp://localhost:8000/mcp--mcp-url
+

The persisted profile is stored at +~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json. You can create or update it from +within the session using /connect.

+

Slash commands + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
CommandDescription
/helpShow all available commands
/statusShow current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status
/connectLaunch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save
/model <name>Hot-swap to a different model mid-session
/mcp <url>Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session
/toolsList the MCP tools the assistant can call
/clearReset conversation history (keeps connection)
/exitQuit the session (also /quit)
+

/connect wizard +

/connect walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:

+
    +
  1. Provider — choose openai, anthropic, local, or other
    2. +
  2. Base URL — preset filled for known providers; override freely
    3. +
  3. API key — input is hidden via getpass
    4. +
  4. Model — sensible default per provider
    5. +
  5. MCP URL — defaults to the current value
    6. +
  6. Save to profile? — writes ~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json so settings persist across sessions
    7. +
+

The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.

+
+

[!NOTE] +Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The customer-outcomes +and connectors commands keep working without one.

+
+

Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes +

Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and +the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a +Job cascades to both.

+
# Jobs
+agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
+agentic-odi jobs list
+agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
+agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
+agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
+
+# Steps (Job Map)
+agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
+agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
+agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
+agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
+
+# Desired Outcomes
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
+agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
+

Add --json to any command for machine-readable output.

+

Evidence +

Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to +a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI +artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.

+
# Capture a record by hand
+agentic-odi evidence add \
+  --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
+  --name "Support lead" \
+  --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
+  --job-id <job-id>
+
+# Read and delete
+agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
+agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
+agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
+
+# Promote into the ODI model
+agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
+agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
+

connectors ingest --job-id <job-id> maps every evidence-bearing record in the +ingested batch into evidence in one step.

+

Schema and scoring +
agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
+agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
+

Manage Customer Outcomes +

Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The local backend +writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add --backend mcp +to route through a running MCP server (python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server). The group is also +available under its historical name outcomes.

+
# Add a Customer Outcome
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
+  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
+  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
+  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
+  --category cost_reduction \
+  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
+
+# Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
+  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
+  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
+  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
+  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
+  --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
+
+# List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
+
+# Get, update, delete
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
+agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
+
+# Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
+agentic-odi score 8 2
+agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
+

score applies the ODI opportunity formula, +importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0).

+

Set AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL (or --mcp-url) to point to a non-default server when +using --backend mcp (default: http://localhost:8000/mcp).

+

Connectors +

The connectors group manages external MCP integrations. See +External Connectors for presets, the connector registry, and +ingest behavior.

+
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+

Updates +

odi update checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by +default; disable it with --no-update for one run or +AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1 globally. See Installation.

+ +

External Connectors (MCP Ingest)

+

The registry, the presets, and the protocol.

+ +
+

Connectors are named integrations stored in .agentic-odi/connectors.json (or a +path you pass with --config / AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE). The first kind is +mcp: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP client and pulls catalog, resources, and +optional tool results from an external MCP server.

+

Presets +

The fastest way to connect is a preset. connectors catalog lists every +built-in preset, grouped by the capability area it serves:

+
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --json
+
+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
Capability area (--area)Presets
Voice of customer & qualitative research (voice-of-customer)notion, gong, fireflies, intercom, confluence
Quantitative data & opportunity scoring (quantitative-data)posthog, amplitude, mixpanel
Market & competitive intelligence (market-intelligence)exa, tavily
Product strategy & backlog alignment (strategy-alignment)linear, github, jira, miro, figma
Strategy & knowledge management output (knowledge-output)slack
+

Register one with --preset; --name defaults to the preset id:

+
# Token-based preset: export the variable it needs first
+export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_...
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+
+# OAuth-based preset: the browser consent flow starts on first use
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
+

Credentials never enter the registry. Presets that use API keys store ${VAR} +placeholders that are resolved from the environment when a connection is +opened, and connectors health names any variable that is missing. --url +overrides the endpoint (self-hosted or proxied deployments) and --tool still +selects which tools to call during ingest.

+

Custom servers keep working the same way:

+
python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
+python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
+
+

[!NOTE] +Presets cover MCP servers with a hosted endpoint. Servers you run yourself +(Snowflake, BigQuery, Google Drive, Brave Search, and similar) are added with +an explicit --url. The catalog lives in +packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py.

+
+
+

[!NOTE] +OAuth tokens are cached in memory for the life of one CLI process, so an OAuth +preset may ask for consent again on the next connectors health or +connectors ingest. Prefer a token-based preset where the server offers one.

+
+

Ingest behavior +

Ingested records are normalized (catalog, resource, tool_result) and +appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are not written into the ODI +jobs/outcomes store — mapping ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts is still on +the roadmap.

+

Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same +Connector protocol later.

+ +

Deployment

+

The project site, the hosted server, and the Worker.

+ +
+

Project Site (GitHub Pages) +

The static site in website/ is published to +https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/ +by .github/workflows/pages.yml.

+
    +
  • A push to main runs the website tests, builds _site from website/, and +deploys the artifact with actions/deploy-pages.
    • +
  • workflow_dispatch republishes the site from the Actions tab without a code +change.
    • +
  • Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source, so there is no +gh-pages branch. Removing pages.yml stops all publishing and the site +returns 404.
    • +
  • The github-pages environment only allows deployments from main.
    • +
+

Hosted MCP Server +

The server is deployed via Horizon Prefect, +Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

+

Test Chat (UI) +

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

+
+

https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat

+
+

MCP Server Endpoint +

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

+
+

https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp

+
+
+

[!IMPORTANT] +Authentication is required to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach +out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a +client.

+
+

Hosted Studio +

The Living Studio SPA is deployed to Cloudflare Workers:

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
EnvironmentURL
Production (main)https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/
Pull request previewPosted automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds as a PR comment
+

Production deploys on every push to main. The Worker is agentic-odi; keep +name in wrangler.jsonc aligned with the Worker connected in the dashboard. +Preview builds run for non-production branches and are ephemeral: the Cloudflare +PR comment is the source of truth, so do not copy a preview URL into docs. The +hosted UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the +sidecar tunnel described below.

+

Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker +

Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on +Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves +the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies /api/* to the sidecar +through a free, account-less +Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.

+

wrangler.jsonc publishes apps/studio/dist with SPA fallback and runs the Worker +first for /api/*; infra/cloudflare/worker.ts forwards those calls to the +SIDECAR_URL secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the +sidecar's CORS list is not involved.

+
# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
+npm --prefix apps/studio ci
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build
+
+# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
+python scripts/dev.py
+
+# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
+cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
+# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints
+
+# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
+npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
+npx wrangler deploy
+

Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
SettingValue
Production branchmain
Root directory/
Build commandnpm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build
Deploy commandnpx wrangler deploy
Preview commandnpx wrangler preview
+

A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set name in +wrangler.jsonc to the Worker you created before the first deploy.

+

Pull request previews +

Workers Builds posts the build status and Preview URL to the pull request +automatically. To enable it:

+
    +
  1. Open the Worker → Settings → Build → Branch control.
    2. +
  2. Keep the production branch set to main and enable Preview Builds.
    3. +
  3. If Cloudflare shows Set up Worker Previews, complete the one-time switch. +This cannot be reversed.
    4. +
  4. Confirm the Preview command is npx wrangler preview.
    5. +
+

wrangler.jsonc must keep a previews block, even an empty one: the +wrangler preview command fails the build with "Your Wrangler configuration is +missing a previews block" without it. Assets and compatibility settings stay +at the top level, so "previews": {} is enough while Previews need no extra +settings. If a future Preview needs vars or bindings, add them under previews +with Preview-safe values.

+

Previews do not inherit production settings. The SPA loads from a Preview, but +/api/* returns 502 SIDECAR_URL is not configured until a preview-specific +SIDECAR_URL secret is configured:

+
npx wrangler preview secret put SIDECAR_URL --name <branch>
+

When --name is omitted it defaults to the current git branch. Previews are +ephemeral, and pull requests from forks may not receive one. If Cloudflare does +not comment, paste the URL into the PR's Deployment section.

+

The cf CLI can inspect build triggers and recent builds (cf builds triggers list, cf builds list) and create a Preview (cf previews deploy), but it does +not post GitHub PR comments. The Workers Builds Git integration owns the PR link; +cf is only an optional verification tool and requires cf auth login.

+
+

[!NOTE] +The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while +python scripts/dev.py and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs +change on every restart — update the secret with +npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL. Chat also needs a reachable +OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's Settings; the canvas, job map, +and impact simulation work without one.

Development

+

Lint, types, frontend checks, and the coverage map.

+

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

Linting, Formatting & Type Checks +

Shared tooling lives in the root pyproject.toml, so one command covers every +Python project:

+
uv run ruff check .
+uv run ruff format --check .
+uv run mypy apps packages
+uv run --directory website mypy .
+
+# Security scanning
+uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
+

Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio) +

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint

+npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
+cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check

Website Checks (GitHub Pages) +

The website/ static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the +committed OG art is reproducible, that index.html stays in sync with the +README, and that the publish pipeline (website/tests/test_pages_deploy.py) +still exists:

Formatting workflow +
    +
  • +

    When editing Python files, either rely on the pre-commit hooks below +(recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

    +
    uv run ruff format .
+
    • +
  • +

    CI behavior:

    +
      +
    • CI runs uv run ruff check . to lint without modifying files.
      • +
    • CI runs uv run ruff format --check . to verify formatting only.
      • +
    • If CI fails on formatting, run uv run ruff format . locally, commit the +changes, and push again.
      • +
    +
    • +
+

Pre-commit hooks +

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

+
uv tool install pre-commit
+pre-commit install
+

After this, ruff and ruff-format run on staged files whenever you commit. +You can also trigger them manually:

+
pre-commit run --all-files
+

Testing +

Tests use pytest with pytest-asyncio (strict mode) and run entirely +in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they +cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

+
uv run pytest                        # everything
+uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
+uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
+uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
+uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
+

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with +packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py, so add or change a tool in +both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps _LOCAL_HANDLERS aligned +with the same tool names.

+

Test Coverage +

CI runs the suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 and uploads one combined +coverage.xml from the 3.12 job to +Codecov.

+

The Codecov upload authenticates with the CODECOV_TOKEN repository secret and +is non-blocking (fail_ci_if_error: false), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR +without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README +tracks main, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

+
    +
  • Project status requires at least 90% coverage (target: 90%) and +tolerates a 1% dip from codecov.yml.
    • +
  • Patch status is informational for now, so new code can land while the +suite catches up.
    • +
+

To reproduce the report locally:

+
uv run pytest \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
+  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
+  --cov-report=term-missing \
+  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
+
+

[!NOTE] +Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. apps/studio/ and test +directories are excluded in codecov.yml.

+
+

Conventions +
    +
  • Test files live under each project's tests/ directory and are named +test_*.py.
    • +
  • Root tests/ is reserved for cross-package checks (contract/ and +scripts/).
    • +
  • Every async test is decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio.
    • +
  • Use Client(mcp) directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
    • +
  • The MCP server's reset_db autouse fixture clears in-memory state before +each test.
    • +

Installation

+

Binaries, the installer, and updates.

+ +
+

Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install the latest +release with one command:

+
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
+

The installer places the binary under ~/.local/share/agentic-odi/versions/<version>/, +creates a current symlink, and symlinks odi, odipm, odi-cli, and +agentic-odi into ~/.local/bin/.

+

If ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH, add it (e.g., +export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"). On Windows, the PowerShell installer +uses ~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\ and copies .exe files to +~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\bin\.

+

Update +

By default, odi auto-checks for updates once every 24 hours and applies the +update on the next run (auto-update is enabled by default). Control behavior +with:

+
    +
  • odi update — explicit check and update
    • +
  • --no-update flag — skip auto-update for this run
    • +
  • AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1 — disable auto-update globally
    • +
+

When running from a non-frozen source install, auto-update is suppressed +automatically.

+

Install layout +
~/.local/share/agentic-odi/
+  ├── versions/<version>/
+  │   └── odi (and bundled files)
+  └── current -> versions/<version>
+
+~/.local/bin/
+  ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi
+  ├── odipm
+  ├── odi-cli
+  └── agentic-odi
+
+~/.config/agentic-odi/  # state/preferences
+

Environment variables: AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR (override install root), +XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_BIN_HOME. The default backend is local +(--backend local); no MCP server is required.

+

Unsigned binaries +

macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries: +xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi (if needed). Windows SmartScreen +may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you +trust the release.

+

Release automation +

Releases are cut and published by CI with no approval step:

+
    +
  1. Conventional commits land on main; release-please opens or updates the +release PR.
    2. +
  2. The release-please workflow arms auto-merge on that PR. main requires the +CI green check (ruleset main-requires-ci-green), so the PR merges itself +as soon as CI passes — nobody clicks merge.
    3. +
  3. The merge cuts tag vX.Y.Z and the GitHub Release; the tag starts the +release and Tauri Release workflows, which attach the CLI archives, +checksums.txt, the install scripts, and the desktop bundles to it. +The release-instructions job then appends an end-user "## 📦 Download & +Run" section to the release page, listing the per-platform archives, +checksums.txt, and the install scripts, plus one-line install and +quick-run commands (idempotent on re-runs).
    4. +
  4. e2e-install runs after release succeeds and installs the published binary +on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
    5. +
+

One-time setup (GitHub App). GitHub holds workflow runs that start from +GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes ("This workflow requires approval from a +maintainer") and ignores the tag such a push creates, which is why releases used +to need a maintainer. A release-only GitHub App avoids both:

+
    +
  1. Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App, with +permissions: Contents Read and write, Issues Read and write, Pull +requests Read and write (no webhook).
    2. +
  2. Install the App on this repository.
    3. +
  3. Add repository secrets RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID (the App's client ID) +and RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY (a generated private key).
    4. +
+

Until those secrets exist, the release-please workflow logs a warning and falls +back to GITHUB_TOKEN: releases still happen, but the release PR needs a +maintainer approval and merge, and the tag will not start the asset builds. After +adding the secrets, re-run the workflow (gh workflow run release-please.yml) or +push to main so the open release PR is re-driven by the App.

+

To check the installer without cutting a release, run +bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh — it serves a simulated release over HTTP and +exercises scripts/install.sh end to end (CI runs it too).

Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend

+

Running a local model with tool calling.

+ +
+

To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a +local LLM backend that:

+
    +
  • Exposes an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API (for example, +/v1/chat/completions), and
    • +
  • Supports OpenAI-style tools / tool_calls.
    • +
+

A simple fully local option is +llama-cpp-python, which can run +a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.

+

1. Install a local LLM server +

Install llama-cpp-python in your environment (see its README for +platform-specific build notes):

+
pip install llama-cpp-python
+

2. Download a small tools-capable model +

Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a +7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. +C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf.

+

3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server +

Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default +used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:

+
python -m llama_cpp.server \
+  --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
+  --model_alias local-tools-model \
+  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
+  --chat_format openai
+

This exposes an OpenAI-style API at http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1.

+

4. Configure the Studio +

The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment +variables (with sensible defaults):

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
VariableDefault
AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URLhttp://localhost:8001/v1
AGENTIC_ODI_MODELlocal-tools-model
AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URLhttp://localhost:8000/mcp
AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEYlocal
+

You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's +Settings panel.

Running The Living Studio

+

The chat-first interface, its first run, and the desktop app.

+ +
+

The Living Studio is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation: +an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact +Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent +connected to the MCP server.

+

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve +the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on http://127.0.0.1:8100 — the +SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

+

Architecture +
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐

+│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
+│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
+└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
+                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
+                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
+                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
+                                                             ▼
+                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
+                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
+                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
+                                                             ▲

+

Interface +

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
SurfaceWhat it does
First-run tourA four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which of four starting points you want, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. Finishing opens the chosen surface; Name the job hands off to the context conversation. Replay it from Settings → Replay the welcome tour.
First runA short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and Explore on my own always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with /start, the home stage's context pill, or Settings.
HeroOne rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or what the studio can do. It cycles every few seconds and stays still under prefers-reduced-motion.
Suggestion pillsBelow the headline. Some start a conversation (define a job, simulate a bet, capture what a customer said), others open a lens (landscape, job map). They change as the canvas fills up.
ComposerDocked at the bottom of the transcript. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Cmd/Ctrl+K focuses it, and / opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams.
BarThe only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread.
RailAbove the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: Landscape · N, Job map · N, Evidence · N. Every item is derived from the canvas, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu.
LensA view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; Esc, Close, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — Ask which to chase, Walk me through the job, Weigh the evidence — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens.
+

Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code). +Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.

+

Type / to open the palette. Up/Down move, Enter or Tab runs the +selected command, Esc closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call +the model, so they work when it is offline.

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +

Unknown commands produce a transcript notice pointing at /help.

+

The welcome tour +

The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is +skippable at every step (Skip the tour or Escape), resumable (progress is +stored after every transition in localStorage["studio.onboarding"]), and +replayable from Settings.

+

Guidance, not gates +

The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the +home stage keeps a dashed Tell me what you're building pill; it reopens the +conversation exactly where you left off. /start and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a +natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts +instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review +and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.

+

Without a model +

When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:

+
    +
  • A Working by hand strip explains the state and offers capture, job map, +and context.
    • +
  • Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled +Local guidance.
    • +
  • Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed; +outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same +local repository the model uses.
    • +
  • Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.
    • +
+

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from +the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

+

The thread is the room +

Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront +never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the +customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that +carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for +doing the work.

+

That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every +artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each +reply with the next move as an action on the surface.

+

Rich responses +

The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a +paragraph, the agent renders one inline in the conversation: a scored +outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a +customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, or a decision record. +Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:

+
    +
  • The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA. +apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts declares nine primitives and six cards, their +JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no +eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same +Markdown component the transcript already used.
    • +
  • The sidecar is catalog-agnostic. The SPA sends the catalog with each turn; +the sidecar derives the render_ui tool schema from it, validates what comes +back, and streams a ui SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool +result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a +fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog +never sees the tool.
    • +
  • Cards are views, never actors. Every button is an intent string that the +agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
    • +
+

A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:

+
{
+  "type": "outcome-card",
+  "props": {
+    "id": "O-1",
+    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
+    "importance": 9,
+    "satisfaction": 3
+  }
+}
+

The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a delta appends to the +open prose part, a ui event opens a card, and the next delta opens a new +paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and +satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home +(src/lib/odi.ts). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree +that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.

+

Adding a surface +
    +
  1. Add an entry to CATALOG in apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts — props as a +JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
    2. +
  2. Register the component in apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts.
    3. +
  3. Implement it in apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx (domain shape) or +apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx (composition).
    4. +
  4. Run npm --prefix apps/studio test. The registry parity test fails if the +catalog and the registry drift apart.
    5. +
+

No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

Desktop signing & updater secrets +

Self-updating and code signing are env-driven: if a secret is absent, an +unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub +Actions secrets.

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
SecretPurpose
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEYSigns updater artifacts (.sig) and the latest.json manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate.
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORDPassword for the private key (optional when the key has none).

+

Releases are published by .github/workflows/tauri-release.yml when a v* tag +is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via +Settings → Check for updates.

+

Managing the updater signing key +

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can +verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The public key is +embedded in apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (plugins.updater.pubkey) and is +safe to commit. The private key must never be committed, logged, printed in +CI, or attached to a build artifact.

+
    +
  1. +

    Generate a key pair (only if you need a new one). Leave -p "" for a +passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

    +
    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
+

    This writes living-studio.key (private, 0600) and living-studio.key.pub +(public).

    +
    2. +
  2. +

    Paste the public key into apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:

    +
    {
+  "plugins": {
+    "updater": {
+      "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
+      "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
+    }
+  }
+}
+
    3. +
  3. +

    Store the private key outside the repository (the repo root is +git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

    +
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
+mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
+chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
+

    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/ +Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives. +Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing +installs.

    +
    4. +
  4. +

    Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret (Settings → Secrets and +variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

    +
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
+gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
+
    5. +
  5. +

    Verify the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

    +
    gh secret list
+
    6. +
  6. +

    Rotate by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the +new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into +their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public +key ahead of the cut-over.

    +
    7. +
+
+

[!CAUTION] +If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new +pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:146-157` (jobs), `:191-205` (steps), `:239-263` (outcomes), `:266-280` (patch outcome) — each calls `call_mcp_tool` and unconditionally returns `{"ok": True, "result": <string>}`.

The MCP server returns failures as **strings**, not exceptions (`apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:114` — `"Error: Job with ID … not found."`, `:118` — `"Error: importance and satisfaction must be between 1.0 and 10.0"`). So the sidecar wraps an error message in `ok: true` and hands it to the SPA as a success.

**The CLI already solves this.** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:545-559` — `_parse_remote` raises `BackendError` if the text starts with `"Error:"` or contains `" not found:"`. The sidecar does not. The same repo, two answers.

**2. The chat stream dies without an event.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:259-276`:
- `mcp_client.list_tools()` at `:259-260` is not wrapped in `try/except`. If the MCP server is down, the `async with McpClient(...)` raises **after** `status: mcp_tools` has already been streamed. The SSE stream dies mid-flight with no `error` event.
- The LLM completion call at `:270` is not wrapped either.
- The MCP server is **never health-checked in the chat path** — only the LLM is (`chat.py:239-240` → `probes.check_llm_health`). The agent can announce "I found the tools" and then fail on the first one.

**3. The connector error event is dropped by the client.**
The sidecar emits `{"status": "error", "error": ...}` (`chat.py:182`). The client reads only `event.data.preset ?? event.data.name` (`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:768-770`) — **both are absent on the error path**, so the id is `""` and the event is discarded. **A failed connector registration is completely invisible to the person.**

**4. The connector list goes stale.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:767-775` — the `connector` event does not call `refreshConnectors()`. The list only refreshes when the person dismisses the suggestion chip (`Composer.tsx:157`) or at boot (`:862`). Settings can show a stale list indefinitely.

**5. A canvas failure is dressed as an empty result.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:515-531` — on error, `canvasLoading` is false and `canvas` stays null. The render condition is `canvasLoading && !canvas`, so the skeleton never shows, and `OpportunityLandscape` renders a metrics grid of zeros plus *"No opportunities match the current filter criteria."* (`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:101-102,161-187`). **An error is shown as an empty result.**

**6. The skeleton is unreachable on a warm start.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:270` — the canvas is restored from `localStorage` at init, so `canvas` is non-null, so `canvasLoading && !canvas` is false and the skeleton never appears. The person sees stale data during a refresh with no indication that a refresh is happening.

**7. The assistant can fail with no reply at all.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:798-816` — if the stream errors before any content, `sendMessage` pops the empty assistant message and the person is left with their own message and no answer — only a toast, which auto-dismisses after 6 s (`:343-345`).

**8. Silent error swallowing in the client.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:364-370` — the connector catalog fetch error is swallowed. `SettingsPanel` renders an empty `<select>` with no explanation (`:151-200`).

**9. `DirectCapture` has no inline error state.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx:47-64` — a failed submit clears nothing and shows only a toast.

**10. The workspace lens has no error boundary.**
`apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkspacePanel.tsx:72-74` — a throw inside a panel bubbles to the app-level `ErrorBoundary` (`apps/studio/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:22-37`), which offers only *"Reload the studio"* — losing the whole session. The per-node `NodeBoundary` (`apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx:53-64`) protects agent-composed surfaces but not the panels.

**11. The tool-round cap truncates silently.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:26` — `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 3`. When the loop exits because of the cap, it emits a `message` with the accumulated prose (`:373`) and the model never gets to answer after its third tool call. The person sees no explanation.

**12. Two routes skip the MCP URL guard.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:196` and `:244` — `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` pass `body.mcp_url` straight to `call_mcp_tool`, while every other route uses `_require_mcp_url` (`:55-58`, `:166`, `:213`, `:271`). An empty URL yields a confusing 502 instead of a 400.

**13. Health is probed once and never again.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:864-881` — the bar shows "Local mode" forever if the model comes up later. Only the wizard's readiness step re-probes (`apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx:57-71`).

## What a person experiences

You ask the agent a question. The MCP server is not running. Instead of the answer simply stopping, the conversation shows, in place, a small panel: *"I could not reach the ODI server at http://localhost:8000/mcp. Your question was saved. Start the server and try again."* — with a **Retry** button that re-runs the turn. If the sidecar cannot reach the LLM, the same panel says *"The model at http://localhost:8001/v1 is not responding."* and offers to switch to the local model. If a save fails because the outcome is malformed, the form says exactly which field is wrong and shows the fix. **Nothing fails quietly, and nothing is dressed up as success.**

## Specification

### 14.1 A single error vocabulary

Create `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/errors.py`:

```python
class StudioErrorCode(StrEnum):
    MCP_UNREACHABLE = "mcp_unreachable"
    MCP_TOOL_FAILED = "mcp_tool_failed"
    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
    LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED = "llm_tool_rounds_exhausted"
    NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
    VALIDATION = "validation"
    OUT_OF_RANGE = "out_of_range"
    CONFLICT = "conflict"
    INTERNAL = "internal"

class StudioError(BaseModel):
    code: StudioErrorCode
    message: str            # plain language, addressed to the person
    detail: str | None = None      # the technical text, for a disclosure
    suggestion: str | None = None  # the next step
    retryable: bool = False
    request_id: str | None = None
```

- The MCP server's string-error convention is preserved at the tool boundary. The sidecar **parses** the string and converts it into a `StudioError` with a code, a suggestion, and a `retryable` flag.
- The parser replaces the CLI's ad-hoc sniffing (`backend.py:545-559`) and is shared by the sidecar and the CLI. **Move it into `packages/core` so both use one implementation** — `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py::parse_tool_result(text) -> StudioError | None`.
- Every HTTP error response in the sidecar uses the same body shape, so the SPA has **one** error path.

### 14.2 The sidecar must not report errors as successes

- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:146-157`, `:191-205`, `:239-263`, `:266-280` — when `call_mcp_tool` returns a string that parses as an error, the route must return the appropriate HTTP status with the `StudioError` body:
  - `not found` → `404`
  - `out of range` / `validation` → `422`
  - `mcp_unreachable` → `502` with `retryable: true`
  - otherwise → `500`
- `{"ok": true}` is removed from these responses. The response **is** the result.
- `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` (`:196`, `:244`) must call `_require_mcp_url` like every other route, so an empty URL is a `400`, not a confusing `502`.

### 14.3 The chat stream must never die silently

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:235-373`:

- **Health-check the MCP server before advertising its tools.** Probe it alongside the LLM at `:239-240`. If it is unreachable, emit `status: "mcp_unreachable"` and return a `message` that says so — do not open the client, do not list tools, do not pretend.
- **Wrap every step of the loop in `try/except`:**
  - the `McpClient` construction and `list_tools()` (`:259-260`);
  - the LLM completion call (`:270`);
  - each `call_tool` (`:313-367`).
- **A fatal error emits an `error` SSE event** before the stream closes, with the `StudioError` body. The stream must always end with either a `message` or an `error` — never both, never neither.
- **The tool-round cap must be explained.** When the loop exits because of `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, the sidecar emits a `message` that includes: *"I reached the limit of 3 tool rounds for this turn. Here is what I have so far — ask me to continue and I will pick up from here."* A cap that truncates without saying so is a lie by omission.
- A tool error that the model can recover from stays a tool result (the current behavior at `:354-358` is right) — but the error is also recorded in the turn's log with the `request_id`.

### 14.4 The client must show failures, and must not drop them

`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:717-782` — the SSE dispatcher:

- **Handle the `error` event.** Currently `apps/studio/src/api/sse.ts:10-46` synthesizes an `error` event on malformed JSON, but the sidecar never sends one. Add a real `error` handler that renders an inline failure panel in the transcript — not a toast, because a toast auto-dismisses (`:343-345`) and the failure is the last thing the person needs to see.
- **Handle the connector error event.** `StudioContext.tsx:767-775` — read `event.data.error` when `event.data.status === "error"` and surface it. Today it is dropped because the handler only reads `preset` and `name`.
- **Call `refreshConnectors()` after any connector event**, so the list is never stale.
- **Do not pop the assistant message when the stream fails.** `:798-816` — keep a failed assistant turn in the transcript with the failure panel, and keep the person's question. A failure that erases the conversation is the worst possible failure.
- **Re-probe health periodically.** Add a poll — every 30 s while the window is focused, and on `visibilitychange` — that calls `POST /api/health/mcp` and `POST /api/health/llm`. The top bar's status must be able to change from "Local mode" to "Connected" without a reload.

### 14.5 Distinct empty states, and no error-as-empty

The rule: **an empty result and a failure are different, and the interface must never show one when the other is true.**

- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:515-531` — the canvas state must be a discriminated union, not four loose booleans:
  ```ts
  type CanvasState =
    | { kind: "loading" }
    | { kind: "ready"; data: CanvasData }
    | { kind: "empty"; data: CanvasData }
    | { kind: "error"; error: StudioError };
  ```
  - `loading` → the skeleton (`apps/studio/src/components/Skeletons.tsx`).
  - `ready` → the content.
  - `empty` → *"No opportunities yet. Tell me the job your customers are trying to get done."* — the empty state must be **an invitation**, not a zero-filled metrics grid.
  - `error` → the failure panel with a **Retry** button.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:101-102,161-187` — the zero-filled metrics grid must only render for a genuinely empty result, never for an error.
- **The skeleton must appear on a refresh**, even with a warm cache. The current condition `canvasLoading && !canvas` (`:515`) is wrong; use the union.
- `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/panels.tsx:34-98` and `WorkspacePanel.tsx:72-74` — every lens gets its own error boundary, so a throw in one panel shows a panel-level failure with a Retry, not a whole-app "Reload the studio" that destroys the session.

### 14.6 Forms must show their errors in place

- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx:47-64` — add an inline error state per field, driven by the `422` body from the sidecar. The `suggestion` from the server is shown next to the field.
- `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:151-200` — a failed catalog fetch renders an explicit error with a Retry, not an empty `<select>`.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:364-370` — stop swallowing the error; surface it.

### 14.7 One request id, one log line, one trail

- Generate a `request_id` per chat turn and per API request, at the edge.
- Log **one structured line per turn**, at the end:
  ```json
  {"ts": "…", "level": "info", "event": "chat_turn", "request_id": "…",
   "model": "local-tools-model", "rounds": 2, "tool_calls": 3,
   "tool_errors": 1, "duration_ms": 1840, "outcome": "completed"}
  ```
  `outcome` is `completed`, `failed`, `partial`, or `rounds_exhausted`.
- The same `request_id` must appear in the MCP server's log line, in the `Execution` record (#82), and in the SSE events for that turn.
- **Never log the token, the API key, or the contents of a tool result that may contain customer data.** Redact by key name at the logger boundary, and test it.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **Every failure reaches the person.** There is no path where the app fails and the person is not told.
- **An error is never rendered as an empty result, and never rendered as success.**
- Every stream ends with exactly one of `message` or `error`.
- The `request_id` is present on every log line, on every SSE event, and on every `Execution`.
- No secret and no customer data is written to a log line.
- The sidecar and the CLI share one tool-result parser.
- The failure panel offers a **Retry** that re-runs the turn, not only a description.

## Out of scope

- Authentication — #90.
- The audit trail — #82.
- Structured logging as a general observability system; this issue introduces the minimum needed to make failures diagnosable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `StudioError` and `StudioErrorCode` exist in `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/errors.py`, and every HTTP error uses that shape.
- [ ] The tool-result parser lives in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py` and is used by both the sidecar and the CLI.
- [ ] The sidecar no longer returns `{"ok": true}` around a tool error; the routes return 404 / 422 / 502 / 500 as appropriate.
- [ ] `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` use `_require_mcp_url` and return 400 on an empty URL.
- [ ] The chat path health-checks the MCP server before advertising its tools.
- [ ] The `McpClient` construction, `list_tools()`, the LLM completion call, and each `call_tool` are all wrapped; a fatal error emits an `error` SSE event.
- [ ] Every stream ends with exactly one of `message` or `error`.
- [ ] Hitting `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` produces a message that says the limit was reached.
- [ ] The client handles the `error` event and the connector error event, and neither is dropped.
- [ ] `refreshConnectors()` runs after any connector event.
- [ ] A failed stream keeps the person's question and shows a failure panel with a Retry; the assistant message is not popped.
- [ ] Health is re-probed on an interval and on window focus, and the top bar status can change without a reload.
- [ ] The canvas state is a discriminated union with `loading` / `ready` / `empty` / `error`; an error never renders the zero-filled metrics grid.
- [ ] The skeleton appears during a warm refresh.
- [ ] Every lens has its own error boundary with a Retry; a panel throw never reaches the app-level boundary.
- [ ] `DirectCapture` and `SettingsPanel` show their errors in place, with the server's suggestion.
- [ ] One structured log line per chat turn, with the `request_id`, the tool count, the error count, the duration, and the outcome.
- [ ] A redaction test proves that a token, an API key, and a customer quote are not written to the log.
